## Recent Papers Found

**1. "Doing More With Less: Revisiting the Effectiveness of LLM Pruning for Test-Time Scaling"**

This paper by Ocean Monjur, Shahriar Kabir Nahin, and Anshuman Chhabra from the University of South Florida compares structured and unstructured pruning approaches. The study shows that unstructured pruning augments TTS (test-time scaling) performance compared to structured pruning, and at times can even outperform unpruned full-weight LLMs. The experiments evaluate model configurations with different structured and unstructured pruning methods at various thinking token limits.

**2. "MUSTAFAR: Promoting Unstructured Sparsity for KV Cache Pruning in LLM Inference"**

This paper demonstrates that unstructured sparsity significantly improves KV cache compression for LLMs, enabling sparsity levels up to 70% without compromising accuracy or requiring fine-tuning. The research finds per-token magnitude-based pruning as highly effective for both Key and Value caches under unstructured sparsity, surpassing prior structured pruning schemes.

**3. "Týr-the-Pruner: Structural Pruning LLMs via Global Sparsity Distribution Optimization"**

This paper proposes an efficient end-to-end search-based global structural pruning framework that constructs a supernet by applying local pruning across a range of sparsity ratios to determine the optimal sparsity distribution under a target overall sparsity ratio.

These papers represent recent research advances in both structured and unstructured pruning techniques for language models.
